name: Wirewound resistor
kb: Resistance by length and gauge of wire wound on form; repeatable and stable
note: Precision requires consistent wire diameter and tight winding; achromatic winding balances inductance.

name: Carbon composition resistor
kb: Finely divided carbon and binder; cheap and smaller than wirewound
note: Carbon content and binder ratio set resistance; tolerance broader than wirewound but adequate for most circuits.

name: Rheostat sliding contact resistor
kb: Variable resistance by moving contact along resistive track
note: Current path through coil via moving contact; heating limits power; precision determines smoothness.

name: Potentiometer precision voltage divider
kb: Helical or toroidal winding with screw-driven contact; voltage division without drawing significant current
note: Manganin wire has minimal temperature coefficient; screw drive prevents wear on track; enables bridge null detection.

name: Fixed mica capacitor
kb: Stacked mica sheets between foil plates; excellent dielectric and stability
note: Mica splits into thin sheets cleanly; stable temperature coefficient; suitable for RF and timing circuits.

name: Fixed paper capacitor
kb: Paper impregnated with oil between foil sheets, rolled and sealed
note: Oil impregnation lowers losses and increases voltage rating; absorbs water readily so must be sealed; cheap at scale.

name: Electrolytic capacitor aluminium
kb: Thin oxide layer on aluminium foil anodized in ammonia or glycerol solution; large capacitance in small volume
note: Oxide thickness controls voltage rating; only works in one polarity; sensitive to temperature and overvolts; vastly higher C/V than paper capacitors.

name: Variable air-gap capacitor
kb: Parallel plates rotating through fixed plates; capacitance varies by overlap and gap
note: Arc-free air dielectric; tuning smooth and reversible; stray inductance from leads limits RF performance.

name: Air-core inductor coil
kb: Wire wound on insulated form with no core; inductance by geometry alone
note: Inductance scales as turns squared; skin effect at high frequency; useful where DC or variable core losses unacceptable.

name: Iron-core inductor and choke
kb: Wire wound on iron core; current saturation and hysteresis loss but much higher inductance
note: Saturation nonlinearity used for current limiting; core loss scales with frequency; permeability much higher than air.

name: Ferrite and powdered iron core
kb: Soft ferrite from calcined iron oxides or iron powder in binder; high permeability, low eddy loss, stable across temperature
note: Ferrite a ceramic; does not conduct eddy currents like iron sheet; high frequency inductor and transformer cores.

name: Quartz resonator and filter
kb: Piezoelectric quartz plate resonating at MHz or kHz; frequency-selective element
note: Mechanical resonance; Q can exceed 10000; temperature coefficient critical; must be mounted to damp overtones without killing Q.

name: Electromagnetic relay switching contacts
kb: Electromagnet pulls armature to make or break electrical contacts; low power input controls high power load
note: Arc damage and pitting of contacts with AC load; silvering extends life; must account for contact resistance in design.

name: Industrial contactor and motor starter
kb: Large relay for motor control; multiple contacts; arc suppression; thermal overload protection
note: Arc chute prevents sustained arc; overload heater coil; three-phase main contacts plus auxiliary; frame standardization aids design.

name: Knife switch and disconnect
kb: Knife blade on hinge makes hard contact with clips; manual on-off
note: No arc suppression; safe only at voltages below 600V or in oil bath; contact pressure from spring determines resistance.

name: Thermal circuit breaker
kb: Bimetallic strip heats and bends to trip latch; trips at set current
note: Time-current characteristic depends on heater coil; not fast; reset after cooling; can be overridden by sustained high current.

name: Magnetic circuit breaker fast trip
kb: Solenoid pulls latch immediately on fault current; instantaneous protection
note: Can be combined with thermal for dual protection; must dissipate solenoid heat continuously; coordination between devices essential.

name: Fuse and wire element cartridge
kb: Fusible element melts at predetermined current, breaking circuit
note: Melt point set by wire diameter and alloy; cartridge design isolates arc; single-use requires replacement; cost nearly zero.

name: Lightning arrestor and gap protector
kb: Air gap or horn gap connected across line to ground; provides low impedance path for transient
note: Horn gap spreads arc to cool it; prevents sustained arc-over; must be coordinated with fuse or breaker to isolate line if arc grounds.

name: Porcelain pin insulator
kb: Porcelain pin insulator for overhead lines; high voltage creepage path
note: Creepage distance (surface path) more critical than straight-line distance; pollution tracking and salt spray demand careful glaze design.

name: Oil-filled bushing insulator transformer
kb: Conductor passes through bushings at transformer terminals; oil-impregnated paper and porcelain
note: Stress grading with increasing porcelain thickness reduces field; oil cooling improves thermal rating; must handle thermal cycling without cracking.

name: Portable electrical plug and socket
kb: Detachable mated connector with contact safety and intermateability
note: Keying and grounding contacts critical; contact wear and oxidation cause heating; standardization enables interoperability.

name: Printed circuit board etched pattern
kb: Photolithographic pattern on copper foil; chemical or mechanical removal to leave tracks
note: Etching must be selective and reproducible; copper adhesion critical; allows mass assembly; enables high-density interconnect.

name: Air-gap transformer inductive coupling
kb: Two coils loosely coupled through air; impedance transformation low but isolation high
note: Loose coupling limits power transfer; useful for RF and signalling; avoids eddy loss but requires many turns.

name: Shunt-wound dynamo generator
kb: Field coil connected in parallel with armature; load increase strengthens field
note: Self-exciting; voltage drops with load; external load variation affects output; inherently stable at constant speed.

name: Series-wound dynamo generator
kb: Field coil in series with armature load; current through field regulates voltage
note: Voltage rises with load if load resistance drops; dangerous behavior if load suddenly disconnected; stabilised by armature reaction.

name: Compound-wound dynamo self-regulating
kb: Shunt and series field coils on same poles; combines voltage stability with current response
note: Over-compound raises voltage with load; under-compound drops voltage; exact balance requires field connection points adjustment.

name: Alternator with rotating magnetic field
kb: Rotating magnet with stationary armature; brushes only on excitation field, not output
note: Slip rings carry small DC to field; no commutator means no brush wear on power output; AC frequency locks to mechanical speed.

name: Synchronous motor locked to line frequency
kb: Rotor poles lock to rotating magnetic field of stator; runs at exact line frequency when loaded within pull-out torque
note: Must be brought up to speed by starting cage winding; field not self-excited; can operate at leading power factor and improve system power factor.

name: Squirrel-cage induction motor
kb: Short-circuited rotor bars in slots run at speed slightly below synchronous due to slip
note: Torque from electromagnetic induction in rotor; starting current high; rotor skew reduces cogging torque; slot geometry critical for performance.

name: Wound-rotor induction motor adjustable speed
kb: Rotor has external slip rings; external resistance limits starting current and enables speed control
note: Resistor heat at reduced speed; used for high-inertia loads; speed varies with load but controlled resistance keeps current safe.

name: Universal motor AC and DC rated
kb: Series-wound motor with commutator; runs on AC or DC; speed varies with load and frequency
note: Commutation challenges at 50-60 Hz on AC; brush wear in higher air-gap flux field limits life; small portable motors favour this design.

name: Permanent magnet stepper motor
kb: Multi-phase coils pull magnetic rotor to discrete positions; one step per pulse
note: Precise repeatable positioning; holding torque when de-energised; microstepping smooth motion at cost of torque; frequency response limited by inductance.

name: Servo motor with feedback control
kb: Motor with position feedback and closed-loop control; servo law adjusts command
note: Feedback must have minimum lag; damping by proportional term prevents oscillation; used in remote positioning and radar antenna drives.

name: Rotary converter and synchronous converter AC-DC
kb: Combined induction motor stator and DC dynamo rotor; converts AC power to DC
note: Synchronous tie to AC line frequency; commutator ripple frequency same as AC frequency; largely replaced by mercury arc rectifier.

name: Mercury arc rectifier thermionic
kb: Thermionic emission from mercury cathode; conducts only one way; high current capacity
note: Starting requires heated filament or external ignition; arc extinction requires current reversal; phase-shift transformer enables delay control.

name: Metal layer rectifier selenium or copper oxide
kb: Asymmetric conductivity of metal-oxide junction; solid state, no vacuum required
note: Forward voltage drop higher than tube; efficiency adequate for small rectifiers; stack many discs for high voltage; temperature coefficient positive.

name: Three-wire distribution system neutral return
kb: Two outer wires at opposite voltage; neutral wire at half voltage to each outer; halves wire mass for same power
note: Neutral current must be zero if balanced; imbalance heats neutral and creates voltage shift; lightning strike on one phase dangerous.

name: Ring main distribution and loop network
kb: Distribution loops back to supply; allows isolating section without losing power to whole ring
note: Fault location critical; relay must see direction of fault current; current sharing unequal; network analysis complex.

name: Primary substation and voltage regulation
kb: Transforms high transmission voltage to lower distribution voltage; tap changer adjusts ratio under load
note: Oil cooling essential for power transformers; tap changer must switch under load without arc; protection coordination paramount.

name: Load tap changer under load
kb: Motor-driven switch selects transformer tap ratio while load still connected
note: Arcing at tap change must be managed; some designs use reactor to limit current during transition.

name: Differential protective relay overcurrent
kb: Compares current in and current out; trips if difference exceeds threshold; protects transformer windings
note: Requires precise current transformer matching; time-delay prevents transient nuisance trips; restraint coil stabilises for magnetising inrush.

name: Earthing and grounding electrode system
kb: Low-resistance path to ground; protects personnel from neutral shift and lightning
note: Resistance depends on soil conductivity and electrode depth; seasonal variation significant; multiple electrodes reduce impedance.

name: Power factor correction and reactive power compensation
kb: Capacitor in parallel with inductive load shifts phase angle toward unity; reduces transmission losses
note: Capacitor must be switched in steps to track load; resonance with line inductance dangerous; overshooting power factor wastes power.

name: Synchroscope phase angle indicator
kb: Two-phase motor runs fast when voltages out of phase; pointer speed and direction indicate phase angle
note: Operator closes paralleling switch when pointer is in fast-slow band; faster than stopping paralleling autotransformer for phase check.

name: Load dispatch center and system scheduling
kb: Central control station directs power plant output to match demand; communication to remote plants
note: System frequency is barometer of balance; shortage lowers frequency, surplus raises it; operator must manually adjust generation.

name: Standardised nominal voltage and tolerance
kb: Agreement on supply voltage: 110V or 230V single phase, 380V three-phase; allows interchangeable equipment
note: Early systems had wild variance 100-250V; voltage drop in line means stepping up at source; tolerance band 10% critical for motor starting.

name: Standardised frequency 50 Hz and 60 Hz
kb: Agreement on AC frequency: 50 Hz in continental Europe, 60 Hz in Americas; locks synchronous motors to line frequency
note: Choice was engineering and politics; once locked in, changing impossible without grid shutdown; early asynchronous generators failed to synchronise.

name: Moving coil milliammeter and voltmeter
kb: Coil moving in field; deflection proportional to current; damping spring prevents oscillation
note: Current through coil creates torque; permanent magnet must be strong; Shunt resistor for ammeter, high series resistor for voltmeter.

name: Moving iron meter fixed scale
kb: Iron vane moves in non-uniform field; deflection approximately proportional to current squared
note: Works on AC and DC; square-law response means scale is crowded at low end; cheaper than moving coil; less sensitive to overload.

name: Electrodynamometer and wattmeter
kb: Two coils: fixed carries load current, moving carries proportional current; deflection is product, hence power
note: Accuracy requires coil geometry; temperature drift in springs significant; must measure true power, not volt-amperes.

name: Energy meter integrating wattmeter
kb: Aluminium rotor torque proportional to power; gear train integrates into kWh readout
note: Billing requires reproducible accuracy; must handle leading and lagging power factor; rotor speed calibrated to meter constant.

name: Megger insulation resistance tester
kb: Hand-cranked generator applies DC voltage; measures leakage resistance
note: Portable field measurement of cable and winding condition; meter coil shunted by unknown resistance giving logarithmic response.

name: AC impedance bridge and LCR bridge
kb: AC source; four-arm bridge with null detector; unknown impedance from balance condition
note: Accuracy depends on standard elements; frequency dependent; Q measurement by additional measurement or by ratio of R and L.

name: Weston standard cell voltage reference
kb: Cadmium-mercury amalgam negative, mercurous sulfate positive; EMF 1.0186V at 20C
note: Shielded from light and vibration; electrodes in saturated sulfate solution; used to calibrate voltmeters; temperature coefficient -0.0000406V/K.

name: Standard resistor manganin coil
kb: Manganin wire has minimal temperature coefficient and stable value
note: Calibrated against international standard; typical accuracy 0.01%; stored in constant-temperature enclosure.

name: Potentiometer method voltage comparison
kb: Unknown voltage balanced against known by adjusting potentiometer; null condition indicates equality
note: No current drawn from unknown source; used to compare EMFs and measure internal resistance; accuracy limited by potentiometer linearity.

name: Ballistic galvanometer pulse integration
kb: High inertia permits coil swing to measure total flux linkage change
note: Must measure total swing angle; temperature coefficient of spring critical; used to measure transformer turns ratio and core losses.

name: Oscillograph string galvanometer pen recorder
kb: Fine conducting string in strong field; pen records displacement on moving paper
note: DC coupled; bandwidth limited by string inertia; essential for transient and power system measurements; requires continuous paper supply.

name: Cathode ray oscilloscope CRO
kb: Electron beam deflected by electric or magnetic field; shows waveform on phosphor screen
note: First practical CRO circa 1930s; sweep generator must have linear time base; persistence of phosphor crucial for observation.

name: Thermionic valve voltmeter high impedance
kb: Triode cathode follower draws negligible grid current; high input impedance
note: Measures voltage without loading circuit; DC-coupled version drifts; AC-coupled for AC signals; useful for high-impedance transducers.

name: Diode thermionic tube rectifier
kb: Heated filament emits electrons; plate collects them; blocks reverse current
note: Soft vacuum has gas ionisation current; hard vacuum preferred; anode heat limits rectification current; used in high-frequency radio reception.

name: Triode amplifying vacuum tube
kb: Grid between filament and plate controls electron current; small voltage change controls large plate current
note: De Forest's 1906 audion; low internal impedance; positive feedback causes oscillation; feedback via grid-plate capacitance unavoidable.

name: Tetrode suppressor and screen grid tube
kb: Screen grid between grid and plate reduces interelectrode capacitance; suppressor grid reduces secondary emission
note: Screen grid voltage holds secondary electrons off plate; reduces Miller effect; higher gain than triode; screen current dissipation.

name: Pentode output and RF amplifier tube
kb: Added suppressor grid eliminates tetrode kink; remote cutoff possible; higher gains
note: Dominant output tube 1930s onwards; low output impedance suitable for audio; good linearity with suppressor biasing.

name: Beam tetrode output tube high power
kb: Beam forming electrodes focus electron beam; lower plate resistance; higher power than pentode
note: High efficiency suitable for RF and audio final stage; parasitic oscillations at high frequency; requires careful circuit design.

name: Thyratron gas-filled switching tube
kb: Gas breakdown initiated by grid pulse; current continues until anode voltage drops
note: Grid loses control once conduction starts; acts as high-current switch; used for AC control and phase shifting.

name: Photomultiplier single photon detector
kb: Photon releases electron from cathode; cascade through dynodes multiplies current
note: Gain millions; extremely sensitive to light; dark current limits sensitivity; useful for weak light detection and scintillation counters.

name: Klystron microwave amplifier and oscillator
kb: Electron beam modulated by input cavity; power extracted at output cavity
note: Tunable by cavity dimensions; very efficient for continuous wave; used in radar transmitters from 1940s.

name: Magnetron high-power microwave oscillator
kb: Electrons spiral in crossed electric and magnetic fields; oscillate in cavity at microwave frequency
note: Compact very high power source; anode cools quickly in pulsed mode; essential for radar; oscillation frequency determined by cavity geometry.

name: Travelling wave tube linear microwave amplifier
kb: Electron beam interacts with electromagnetic wave on slow-wave structure; gain throughout tube length
note: Distributed interaction gives broad bandwidth; lower efficiency than magnetron; used for satellite and communication links.

name: Photodiode and photoelectric cell
kb: Photons generate electron-hole pairs across junction; small current proportional to light intensity
note: Used for exposure meters and light measurement; selenium cell slower but more sensitive than copper oxide; no amplification stage.

name: Thermistor temperature-sensitive resistor
kb: Oxide resistance decreases sharply with temperature; NTC provides temperature compensation or measurement
note: PTC types also possible; hysteresis in temperature response; good for bias and compensation networks in amplifiers.

name: Varistor voltage-dependent resistor
kb: Resistance decreases sharply above threshold voltage; nonlinear protection element
note: Used for surge suppression and crowbar overvoltage protection; avalanche-like conduction; energy dissipation in transient.

name: Tuned circuit resonance tank LC
kb: Series or parallel LC; impedance minimum (series) or maximum (parallel) at resonance; high Q at resonance
note: Resonant frequency given by 1/(2*pi*sqrt(LC)); quality factor Q equals reactance at resonance divided by resistance.

name: Resonance and Q factor frequency selectivity
kb: Bandwidth equals resonant frequency divided by Q; high Q means sharp selectivity
note: Energy storage in L and C reactances Q times energy dissipated per cycle; Q limited by resistance in practical circuits.

name: RC low-pass and high-pass filters
kb: Time constant RC determines cutoff frequency; one pole rolloff 20dB/decade
note: Low-pass blocks high frequencies; high-pass blocks low frequencies; cutoff at -3dB point where reactance equals resistance.

name: Band-pass and notch filters tuned rejection
kb: Series resonant for band-pass in series path; parallel resonant for notch in shunt
note: Bandwidth depends on Q of tuned circuit; notch depth limited by element losses; used for interference rejection in radio.

name: Amplifier stage and gain
kb: Voltage gain equals amplification factor times load impedance; current gain is cathode bias divider dependent
note: Amplification occurs because small grid voltage controls large plate current; coupling network isolates stages and blocks DC.

name: Negative feedback and Blacks 1927 theorem
kb: Output fed back to input in phase opposition; reduces gain but improves linearity and stability spectacularly
note: Black's insight 1927: gain with feedback equals open-loop gain divided by (1 + loop gain); distortion reduced by same factor.

name: Oscillator feedback oscillation and frequency generation
kb: Positive feedback regenerates input; tuned circuit sets frequency
note: Starting from thermal noise; loop gain must exceed unity; crystal oscillator very stable; LC oscillator easily variable frequency.

name: Multivibrator astable and monostable binary circuit
kb: Two cross-coupled amplifiers with capacitor timing; bistable switching or free-running oscillation
note: Astable multivibrator: relaxation oscillator; monostable: one stable state, pulse triggered; chain of multivibrators forms binary counter.

name: Flip-flop latch and binary memory element
kb: Two stable states; external pulse switches state; remains until next pulse
note: SR and JK flip-flops used for sequential logic; race conditions when setting and resetting simultaneously; trigger must be brief.

name: Counter frequency division and binary scaling
kb: Chain of flip-flops divides frequency by powers of two; counting pulses into decades
note: Used in frequency meters and timers; ripple counter has propagation delay; synchronous counter uses common clock.

name: Mixer frequency conversion and translation
kb: Two frequencies mixed in nonlinear device; difference and sum frequencies output
note: Heterodyne conversion; intermediate frequency allows fixed narrowband amplification; mixer loss adds noise figure.

name: Detector and demodulation envelope and product detection
kb: AM envelope detection by rectifier and RC filter; product detection for SSB and CW
note: Rectifier bias sets detection point; high load resistance needed for AM; product detection with local oscillator restores suppressed carrier.

name: Discriminator and FM demodulation
kb: Symmetrical tuned circuits above and below center frequency; output voltage proportional to frequency deviation
note: S-curve characteristic; slope at center provides deviation sensitivity; FM less noise-prone than AM for same bandwidth.

name: Modulator amplitude frequency and phase modulation
kb: AM: varies RF amplitude with modulation; FM: varies RF frequency; PM: varies RF phase
note: AM needs linear amplification; FM needs frequency-stable oscillator; deviation ratio determines bandwidth.

name: Power supply rectification and smoothing
kb: Full-wave rectification; L-C or RC filter removes ripple
note: Capacitor input filter: ripple voltage decreases with size; inductor input: smoother initial voltage rise; transformer secondary voltage higher for same DC.

name: Voltage regulation zener shunt and series regulator
kb: Zener holds constant voltage across load; series regulator controls pass device to maintain output
note: Load regulation depends on output impedance; series regulation improves ripple rejection compared to zener; efficiency loss in pass element.

name: Impedance matching transformer and L-network
kb: Transformer turns ratio or L-network adjusts impedance to maximum power transfer
note: Bandwidth limited for transformer; L-network single frequency; Smith chart aids design; unnecessary if source and load both 50 ohm.

name: Transmission line and coaxial cable propagation
kb: Two-conductor transmission line has characteristic impedance; reflection-less termination at load
note: Velocity factor less than speed of light; skin effect increases loss at high frequency; wavelength determines physical line length.

name: Waveguide rectangular and circular propagation
kb: Metal tube confines electromagnetic wave; lower loss than coax at microwave frequencies
note: Cutoff frequency below which wave does not propagate; multiple modes possible; mode matching required at junctions.

name: Antenna patterns radiation and efficiency gain
kb: Dipole and loop antennas; gain and directivity patterns; impedance matching to feedline
note: Radiation resistance determines efficiency; pattern directivity increases gain; matching network tunes reactance to resonance.

name: Arc welding carbon and metal electrode
kb: High current DC arc melts metal; electrode supplies filler or as shield; heat record high
note: AC welding problematic due to arc extinction each half-cycle; carbon electrode leaves residue; metal electrode suited to steel joining.

name: Resistance welding spot and seam fusion
kb: High current passes through sheets at overlap; resistance heating melts metal
note: Electrode force and cooling critical; pressure timing and current duration must be coordinated; repeatable and no filler needed.

name: Induction heating and inductive coupling
kb: AC current in coil induces currents in metallic workpiece; eddy current heating
note: Frequency determines coupling and penetration depth; high frequency shallow, low frequency deep; no direct contact between heater and load.

name: Dielectric heating capacitor field
kb: High-frequency AC field polarises molecules in insulating material; molecular motion generates heat
note: Uniform heating without contact; suitable for plastics and wood; frequency typically 5-50 MHz; capacitor loss must be managed.

name: Electroplating and electrorefining coating
kb: Cathode reduction deposits metal from solution; anode dissolution provides metal ions
note: Overvoltage for hydrogen evolution must be prevented; bath agitation improves uniformity; purity of plating metal depends on anode dissolution.

name: Electropolishing etching and surface finish
kb: Reverse electroplating: anodic dissolution removes material with smooth finish
note: Polishing action depends on electrolyte composition; mass transport controls smoothness; passivation layer prevents further attack at end.

name: Electrostatic precipitation and dust collection
kb: Strong electric field ionises gas and charges dust particles; particles move to collection electrode
note: Corona discharge maintains ionisation; collecting electrode rapped to dislodge dust; very high efficiency; secondary effects on emissions.

name: Electric locomotive and traction motor
kb: AC induction motor powered from pantograph; speed controlled by frequency and voltage
note: Regenerative braking possible with proper control; efficiency high compared to diesel; requires substantial electrical infrastructure.

name: Trolleybus overhead catenary power distribution
kb: Bus motor powered from overhead two-wire catenary; less power than rail but no track installation
note: Pantograph contact must handle gaps and curves; power loss in catenary cable significant; quiet urban transport advantage.

name: Electric lift motor and gear reduction
kb: Motor with speed reduction and brake; controlled acceleration and deceleration
note: Brake holds car at floors; motor starting torque must be limited; governors prevent overspeed; safety switches on all gates.

name: Electric handheld drill and motor
kb: Universal AC-DC motor in handheld drill with speed control
note: Speed varies with line voltage; brush wear limits life; rechargeable batteries later replace cord power; torque reaction requires two hands.

name: Loudspeaker moving coil magnetic transducer
kb: Voice coil moves in magnetic field; cone amplifies displacement into sound pressure
note: Impedance matching transformer couples line-level signal to speaker; frequency response limited by cone resonance and suspension compliance.

name: Carbon contact microphone transmitter
kb: Sound-driven diaphragm compresses carbon granules; resistance varies with pressure
note: High acoustic output; requires steady biasing current; output impedance low; used in telephone handsets and early broadcast microphones.

name: Dynamic microphone moving coil induction
kb: Coil in field moves with diaphragm; induced voltage proportional to sound velocity
note: Output impedance high; frequency response relatively flat; robust and simple; bidirectional so can be speaker.

name: Condenser microphone electrostatic capacitor
kb: Thin diaphragm moves relative to fixed plate; capacitance variation amplified by high-impedance amplifier
note: Excellent frequency response and low distortion; requires power supply for bias and impedance converter; sensitive to humidity.

name: Ribbon microphone velocity transducer
kb: Thin ribbon suspended in field; velocity-sensitive output; figure-eight polar pattern
note: Very low output impedance; warm sound prized for vocals; fragile to wind and impact; directional pattern used in studios.

name: Telephone exchange switching and network
kb: Electromechanical stepping relays route calls; bank-and-wiper selector or crossbar matrix
note: Dial sends pulses; register interprets digits; selector then hunts for free trunk; crossbar matrix more elegant but slower.

name: Radar pulse modulation and detection
kb: Pulsed RF transmitted; reflected echo received and displayed on CRT with range proportional to time delay
note: Range resolution by pulse width; azimuth by antenna rotation; elevation by antenna tilt; clutter rejection critical; Doppler reveals speed.

name: Sonar acoustic detection and ranging
kb: Ultrasonic pulse transmitted; echo received and time-to-range conversion displays contacts
note: Frequency 20 kHz to MHz for resolution; attenuation in water limits range; multibeam arrays scan volume; target motion analysis reveals speed.

name: Photocell vacuum and gas photoelectric tube
kb: Photons release electrons from photocathode; current proportional to light intensity
note: Gas-filled faster response but shorter life; vacuum phototubes more stable; used for light measurement and object detection.

name: X-ray tube and cathode ray production
kb: Accelerated electrons strike metal target; bremsstrahlung X-rays produced
note: Anode cooling critical; tube life limited by cathode emission; window allows X-ray exit; lead shielding required; radiation safety paramount.

name: Electron microscope electromagnetic lens
kb: Electron beam focused by magnetic lenses; specimen scattering imaged on fluorescent screen or photographic plate
note: Resolution limited by electron wavelength; lens aberrations substantial; requires very high vacuum and stability; used from late 1930s.
